Sobel operator is used to detect the edge of the blocks around the lost block and find the more precise estimation of the motion vectors by all edge blocks. Simulation results show that the proposed method can recover the higher quality image in different video sequences, comparing to the existing traditional concealment algorithms.

articleTitle: Soft-output MMSE MIMO detector under MMSE channel estimation
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In reality, this is no such thing as perfect channel estimation. To improve the performance of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detector under imperfect channel estimation, some novel detectors recently have been proposed by taking the channel estimation errors into account. However, all these existing detectors are with respect to maximal likelihood (ML) MIMO channel estimation. In this paper, a novel soft-output minimum mean square error (MMSE) MIMO detector is proposed with respect to MMSE MIMO channel estimation. This proposed detector takes channel estimation errors into account in the computation of the MMSE filter and LLR of each coded bit, i.e. the soft information. When compared with conventional soft-output MMSE MIMO detector, our simulation results show that the proposed novel detector can remarkably reduce the residual error floor due to the channel estimation errors, while achieving significant performance gain at the cost of negligible increase of complexity. Furthermore, it is observed from our simulation results that the proposed detector is not sensitive to the inaccuracy of channel estimation error statistics. Therefore, it can be a promising candidate to be applied in practical systems.

articleTitle: Hop status estimation algorithm based on coherent demodulation of CPM
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A hop status estimation algorithm and its error recovery scheme combined with RS (Reed-Solomon) codes are proposed for enhancing the error correcting performance of coherent demodulation of Continuous Phase Modulation (CPM) signal in mobile radio frequency hopping channels. The algorithm provides an accurate hop status estimation by fully exploiting the metric weights rendered after recursively searching through the phase trellis of CPM. As a result, the algorithm requires no extra pilot bits and delay. Both simulation and analytical results show that an average of 98.6% accurate estimation probabilities can be achieved for CPM with modulation index h = 1/2. When combined with RS codes, corrupted hops are indicated as erasures. The residual bit error rate is reduced 38.82% and 36.34% under different channel corrupted hop rate (CHR) by fully utilizing the extrinsic information signaled from the demodulator.

articleTitle: Integrated optical magnetic field sensor with a doubly-loaded loop antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, We design a new type of integrated optical sensor to detect the magnetic near-fields. The probe head consists of a LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> optical waveguide modulator and a doubly-loaded loop antenna element. The magnetic field information can be obtained by detecting the output optical intensity. Compared with the traditional magnetic field probes, it has lower disturbance of measured field, and can suppress the electrical influence effectively. The simulation results show that the proposed sensor is suitable for magnetic near fields measurements.

articleTitle: A whole scheme for aircraft target identification in HRRP
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: this paper describes the authors’ efforts in practical high resolution range profile target automatic recognition. The practical high resolution range profile has more difference to simulation results, so this paper presents a novel algorithm to detect and extract the target range profile data and also create a whole scheme to deal with this difference. First it takes OS CAFR and binary accumulation algorithm to detect target. Here we lower self-adapt threshold to get more targets which maybe be false target. Then we use target trace management to remove the illusion target The novel algorithm, called as endpoint detection based on moving window, can get more valuable data to classification. Practical data has more noise and low PSN, so K-mean algorithm can remove the bad data. Due to variation of target high resolution range profile we build a suffice sample set, which require us to use PCA algorithm to reduce the computer time and memory. Classification is N near classifier, which can get a nonlinear classification effect. The test results prove that this scheme can get better recognition results.

articleTitle: Blind SNR estimation with empirical characteristic function’s derivative in high-order modulation system
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In order to retrieve the pre-estimated information from the received signals, it is necessary to estimate the variance of AWGN channel during the initialization of Turbo iterative decoder. Some literature has been devoted to this problem in BPSK/8PSK scenarios, and in this paper, we present another low-complexity blind SNR estimation method based on empirical characteristic function’s derivative. It proves to be effective for both MPSK and MQAM, which alternatively provides a good un-biased estimation at receiver even without the knowledge of modulation type, as we can see in the simulations.

articleTitle: A power-efficient 0.8 V, 9-bit, 20-MS/s pipelined ADC with opamp-shared loading-free architecture
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper demonstrates a 0.8-V, 9-bit, 20-MS/s pipelined ADC with only 0.58 pJ-Volts/step. A novel circuit architecture which merges opamp-sharing with loading-free structure is proposed. Such mechanism effectively reduces the number of opamps as well as the capacitive loading. In addition, an Inverse-Flip-Around sample-and-hold with unity-feedback factor is employed which further reduces the power consumption. Simulation results using a 0.18 μm CMOS 1P6M process demonstrate the power consumption of this pipelined ADC is 4.5 mW which amounts to a figure-of-merit of 0.58 pJ-Volts/step.

articleTitle: Optimal correlation based frequency estimator with maximal estimation range
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The estimation range and estimation accuracy are contradictory in conventional correlation based frequency estimators due to phase ambiguity. A novel frequency estimator is proposed to unwrap the correlation phase sequence through a differential-modulus-accumulation process. By utilizing the whole unwrapped phase sequence, the proposed estimator is able to achieve maximal estimation range with CRB approaching estimation accuracy and low SNR threshold simultaneously. Both analysis and simulation demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed frequency estimator.

articleTitle: Shared protection in multicast optical networks
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of survivable multicasting in wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) optical mesh networks using optical-layer mixed-sharing protection. The term “mixed-sharing” refers to that both the schemes of “self-sharing” and “cross-sharing” are implemented to protect the multicast sessions. Each link on the primary tree(s) of a multicast session engrosses a wavelength channel. Under normal operation, the backup resources do not carry any traffic. So the backup resources of a multicast session may be shared by that of other sessions in the network. In this paper, we formulate an optimization model of the mixed-sharing protection for a batch of multicast sessions. We can obtain the optimal primary trees and their backup resources by solving the formulation. Simulation results show that the scheme of mixed-sharing can improve the performance of protection.

articleTitle: Area & delay driven binding algorithm of RTL tech. mapping for heterogeneous FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Nowadays, FPGA architecture has been improved rapidly, and more and more hard structures are integrated on heterogeneous FPGA chips. RTL technology mapping is one of methods to solve the problem of making use of those hard structures efficiently. However, the traditional RTL mapping tools can not do optimization on the delay on interconnect wires which can not be ignored in the current integrated circuit technology. So this paper focuses on an area and delay trade-off optimization, refers to improved inferring by more complex rules, and make use of simulated annealing algorithm to get a global optimization. The experiment results show our algorithm can give a 10% better optimization on delay.

articleTitle: Distributed amplifier using enhancement-mode AlGaN/GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Distributed amplifiers (DAs) using 1mm-gate enhancement-mode AlGaN/GaN HEMT were designed and fabricated. Design process and Simulation results of the DA are given. Simulation results show the input and output VSWR (voltage standing wave ratio) of less than 2, associated gain of more than 8.5dB and gain ripple of less than 1dB at frequency from 2GHz to 6GHz.

articleTitle: On the maximum likelihood method for target localization using MIMO radars
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radars, which can transmit multiple linearly independent probing signals, have been shown to provide improved performance in theory and practice. We address herein the maximum likelihood (ML) method for target localization and estimation using MIMO radars and propose two approximate ML algorithms. One of the proposed algorithms outperforms the other one at the cost of computational load. The performance of the proposed methods is validated by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Adaptive video coding control for H.264/AVC
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: H.264/AVC standard employs some advanced technologies that can provide high coding efficiency to reduce the video bit-rate. This paper presents an effectively adaptive group-of-picture (AGOP) coding control for H.264/AVC system based on the temporal correlation. We efficiently estimate the parameter of temporal correlation and to decide the quantization scale. The I-frame is adaptively replaced by enhancement P-frame to improve the coding efficiency when the temporal correlation is high. For high-motion sequences, we can fast track the quantization scale for each frame to reduce the quality deviation of inter-frames. Simulation results shows that the proposed algorithm can achieve the improvement about 2.195dB PSNR in average compared with the original H.264/AVC reference software JM10.1.

articleTitle: A platform-based SoC design for a multi-standard audio decoder
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In complex SoC design, the reusable IP is very useful to achieve the whole system with high verification. Based on this issue, a Hardware and Software (HW/SW) co-design approach can obtain maximum performance, and is easily integrated with the other functions to complete the system. This paper presents the multi-standard audio decoder design with hardware/software co-design flow. First we need to generate the deliverable IP as the hardware design part, and then construct the other modules as software design part. In order to save the hardware cost, the hardware accelerator is applied with the fast algorithm and some techniques on architecture design. Not only just an implementation on the complex system design, our design flow can help designer to profile and analyze the performance in system level. With an aid on it, we can provide a multi-standard decoder with hardware accelerator to improve system performance. The implement result shows that it only needs 3.6 MHz in real-time constraint. With this low operation frequency, the multi-standard audio decoder with HW/SW co-design approach can take advantage on low power constrained application, especially on portable device.

articleTitle: A 10-b low-voltage CMOS pipelined analog-to-digital converter
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A 10-b low-voltage CMOS pipelined analog-to-digital converter is described. A low-voltage technique is proposed for pipelined ADC that avoids the use of low-threshold voltage process, on-chip clock voltage doubler, bootstrapped switch, or switched-opamp technique. At the front-end, a low-voltage S/H circuit with cross-coupled input sampling switch is employed to eliminate the input signal feedthrough and enhance the dynamic performance of the pipelined ADC. The cross-coupled configuration of multiplying digital-to-analog converter (MDAC) also provides an effective common-mode feedback to overcome the problem of common-mode accumulation. Simulation results are given to demonstrate the potential advantage of the new technique.

articleTitle: Numerical study of short pulse propagation and switching in active two-core nonlinear fiber couplers
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The propagation and switching of short pulses in an active two-core fiber nonlinear directional coupler have been investigated theoretically by using the numerical simulation method. The analysis highlight the effects of the second order coupling coefficient dispersion, the linear gain coefficient and the finite gain bandwidth on the propagation and switching of short pulses. We demonstrate that with the influences of the second order coupling coefficient dispersion, the linear gain can sharpen the switching characteristic, lower considerably the switching threshold power, as well as increase significantly the switching efficiency. On the contrary, both the second order coupling coefficient dispersion and the finite gain bandwidth, degrade the switching characteristics. The interplay between the second order coupling coefficient dispersion and the linear gain coefficient on pulse propagation can cause pulse periodic fluctuation associated with pulse compression and amplification. Additionally, pulse compression and amplification induced by linear gain can be significantly suppressed by the interplay between the second order coupling coefficient dispersion and the finite gain bandwidth on pulse propagation, consequently, as in the case of the passive fiber coupler, optical pulses tend to restore periodical coupling propagation in active two-core fiber coupler.

articleTitle: An image inpainting technique based on nonparametric kernel estimation
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Image inpainting is an important research topic in image processing and computer graphics, etc. Its objective is to restore the lost information or remove the unnecessary object according to around image information, which can be used to restore old photo, remove text and conceal errors in videos. However, previous algorithms are not to be perfectly performed. In this paper, a new image inpainting algorithm based on nonparametric kernel estimation is presented. From a statistical point of view, the inpainting can be viewed as an estimation problem with the missing data. Firstly, an initial value was estimated by using the known information as Taylor expansion at the missing point. And then a cost function was obtained by utilizing a Gaussion kernel function to penalize the estimate error. Finally, the missing data are restored through minimizing the cost function. Experimental results show that the proposed method can mend a large variety of images effectively and robustly.

articleTitle: A fast ML sphere decoder with multi-layer multi-path search
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Spatial multiplexing is a key feature for upgrading transmission rate in recent wireless communication systems. However, the performance improvement comes at the cost of decoding complexity. Sphere decoders have shown the distinction to provide the maximum likelihood (ML) solution to this signal detection problem with much lower complexity than the exhaustive search. In this paper, the algorithm of a multi-layer multi-path sphere decoder is proposed. The common information of the same signal carried at different layers can be discovered. Moreover, multiple nodes are visited simultaneously to speed up the search process. Meanwhile, the completeness in the whole search space is still retained to derive the ML solution without conflicts among the different search paths. Simulation results show that more than 50% decoding cycles can be reduced and hence the average throughput can be increased.

articleTitle: Image watermarking via sequencing wavelet filters
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: We propose to watermark images based on wavelet filter banks by encoding the watermark bits into the choice of the filters, in contrast to the conventional watermarking schemes. Such filters are selected from different classes in such a way that they lead to sufficiently distinguishing subbands upon different sequence of filters. A partial sorting on a chosen subband to mark the watermark existence is developed to better camouflage the watermark and to fend off certain noise injection attacks. The selection strategy of the subband coefficients for the partial sorting can be user defined and aims to achieve better imperception in the selected band. The watermark detection thus hinges on measuring the deviation of sorted coefficients specifically scattered in a targeted subband. Experiments conducted on still images and video frames show that the proposed scheme is robust to both noises and illumination changes.

articleTitle: Insertion Based Packets Scheduling for providing QoS guarantee in switch systems
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper we propose the Insertion Based Packets Scheduling (IBPS), a novel packet scheduling method which can significantly reduce the maximum packet delay and delay jitter of high priority real-time data in packet switch systems. Traditional packet-by-packet scheduling will block a packet of real-time service in the packet queue until the transmission of a long non-real-time packet is finished if the real-time packet arrives after the beginning of the non-real-time packetpsilas transmission, and therefore has a bad effect on the delay and delay variation of the real-time service. While, in order to provide a better QoS for real-time services, the IBPS allows a real-time packet to be inserted into a non-real-time packet when the latter is being transmitted. IBPS can be applied with any existing packet scheduling algorithm, such as PQ (Priority Queuing) and WFQ etc. We build a prototype switch system, which can use both the IBPS based PQ and traditional packet-by-packet based PQ for packets scheduling, to evaluate the performance of IBPS. Test results of this prototype system show that IBPS based packets schedulers can achieve significantly lower maximum packet delay and delay jitter of real-time service.

articleTitle: Semi-blind iterative receiver for MIMO-OFDM system with multi-tone narrow-band interference
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A joint channel estimation and data detection scheme by using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is proposed for MIMO-OFDM systems with multi-tone narrow-band interference (MTNBI). The channel impulse response, the noise variance and the indicator of the impulse noise can be estimated accurately, and then the receiver knows whether the signal is interfered by the narrow band interference. One of the most attractive advantages of MCMC method is that it can cooperate with soft-input soft-output decoding, and thus it can be used in turbo detection. Simulation results show that the proposed receiver can approach the performance of the receiver with ideal channel state information under the slow fading channel.

articleTitle: High coupling scheme of an elliptical gaussian pattern laser-to-SMF microlens
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The hyperbolic-end microlens has higher coupling efficiency than the hemispherical-end microlens. This study propose the theoretic analysis concerning the optical-field variations of intensity and wavefront in the SMF waveguide both the hyperbolic-end microlens and the hemispherical-end microlens.

articleTitle: Development of fiber based micro wavelength-division multiplexers
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: We demonstrate a micro 980/1550nm wavelength division multiplexer (μWDM). The overall size was less than 2mm×300μm. The wavelength isolation of 1550nm was measured as 8.95dB, being consistent with the simulation result.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of location management for multi-beam GEO Mobile Satellite System
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: An adaptive location management scheme, called as MPA (Mobility Pattern Adaptive) scheme is proposed for the multi-beam GMSS (Geostationary Mobile Satellite System). Compared with the traditional schemes applied in the terrestrial mobile communication systems, a restraining updating strategy will be applied to the low velocity MES (Mobile Earth Station). Additionally, based on the information theory and data mining algorithm, the high velocity MES will establish a location area visiting list and adjust its updating strategy adaptively based on its mobility pattern which is learned from the visiting list. Simulation results show that the MPA location management scheme proposed decreases the signaling cost on location management significantly. Furthermore, this scheme has a favorable adaptability to the MES with various CMR (Call Mobility Ratio) and maintains a fairly low complexity.

articleTitle: New resource management strategy for multi-service mobile wireless cellular networks
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a predictive controller based on adaptive resource management techniques for multi-service wireless cellular networks to keep the handoff failure rate (HFR) below a target value regardless of the traffic dynamics and bandwidth requirements of the service types. In this paper, we propose a modified feedback algorithm to control the reserved resource. Simulations results indicate that this algorithm can maintain target HFR for any service type even when the traffic load rapidly fluctuates and system parameters vary over a wide range. This algorithm has superior performance in terms of total carried traffic.

articleTitle: Modeling of Network Situation Awareness
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Network situation awareness (NSA) is a new idea of network security, it is different from normal network security technique for its visualization and high-level data management, transform the abstract data to knowledge that human can understand, help network manager to make decision. Present NSA model have some weakness donpsilat fit to network security. This paper promote a improve model of the NSA, add privacy-preserving module, richen the data source, visualization (integrate GIS technique) and projection technique of situation awareness to improve abilities of emergences respond, reduce losses of network attacks, reveal abnormally intrusions.

articleTitle: An advanced model for calculating the effective capacitance considering input waveform effect
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In deep submicron designs, predicting gate delays is a noteworthy work for static timing analysis (STA). The effective capacitance C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> concept is usually used to calculate the gate delay of interconnect load. Conventionally, the input-signal is assumed as ramp waveform. However, the input waveform is also the output of CMOS gates with interconnect wires. Thus the simple assumption as a ramp signal results in significant influence on the delay calculating. In this paper, an advanced effective capacitance model is proposed to consider both the input waveform effect and interconnect wire load, where the nonlinear influence of input waveform is modeled as one part of effective capacitance of capacitive load to compute the gate delay. Experimental results show a significant improvement in accuracy when the input waveform effect is considered.

articleTitle: STBC based DS-BPAM UWB communication system
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, based on the Alamouti space time block codes (STBC) and direct-sequence bipolar pulse amplitude modulation (DS-BPAM) ultra wideband (UWB) system, we investigate the STBC based DS-BPAM UWB system over IEEE UWB multipath fading channels. In order to make the benefits of multipath channels, SRake receiver is applied in this paper. Theoretical bit error probability of the STBC based multi-antenna DS-BPAM UWB system is derived and signal processing algorithm is provided. The system performance of the STBC based DS-BPAM UWB system is evaluated through both SRake receiver and conventional coherent receiver. The results show the efficiency of the STBC based DS-BPAM UWB system with SRake receiver over multipath fading channels.

articleTitle: Stability analysis and design for amplifier-based CMOS analog signal processing cells
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper the stability analysis and design are presented for amplifier-based CMOS analog signal and information processing cells. By analyzing the influence of dominant pole of feedback path on the frequency response of feedback circuits, several design criteria are proposed to keep amplifier-based CMOS analog processing cells stable such as divider and square root. Moreover, several methods to avoid oscillation are discussed for amplifier-based CMOS analog signal and information processing cells. To verify the proposed design, test circuits are fabricated using CMOS 0.6 um process and experimental results show that the proposed analysis and design can be used to improve the stability of amplifier-based CMOS analog and information processing cells significantly.

articleTitle: Transient and frequency characteristics of photodetectors and their effects on data receivers in fiber-linked communication systems
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper tries to characterize avalanche photodiodes (APD) in time and frequency domain and to analyze its influences on optical receivers. For this reason a circuit model of PIN-avalanche photodiodes based on carrier rate equations and a 2.5 Gb/s CMOS optical front-end is designed to contemplate the mutual effects of photodetector characteristics and receiver performances.

articleTitle: Fractional chaos based communication systems —an introduction
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: As one of secure communication means, chaotic communication systems has been well-developed during the past three decades. Technical papers, both for theoretical and practical investigations, have reached a huge amount in number. On the other hand, fractional chaos, as a parallel ongoing research topic, also attracts many researchers to investigate. As far as the IT field is concerned, the research on control systems by using fractional chaos known as FOC (fractional order control) has been a hot issue for quite a long time. As a comparison, interesting enough, up to now we have not found any research result related to Fractional Chaos Communication (FCC) system, i.e., a system based on fractional chaos. The motivation of the present article is to reveal the feasibility of realizing communication systems based upon FCC and their superiority over the conventional integer chaotic communication systems. Principles of FCC and its advantages over integer chaotic communication systems are also discussed.

articleTitle: WLS IIR digial filter design using SOCP
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we propose an iterative method for designing IIR digital filters in the weighted least squares (WLS) sense. Since the original design problem is essentially nonconvex, it is first relaxed into a second-order cone programming (SOCP) problem. By solving the relaxed problem, the lower bound on the optimal value of the original problem can be obtained. And the corresponding filter coefficients can be chosen as the starting point of the following iterative procedure. At each iteration, a linear inequality constraint is further incorporated to gradually reduce the gap between the original and the relaxed problem. Analyses show that the convergence of the proposed iterative procedure can be definitely guaranteed. Two examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Algorithms for the measurement of liquid metal coolant flow velocity with correlated thermal signals
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The flow velocity of liquid metal coolant can be determined through the measurements of temperature fluctuation recorded by a pair of temperature sensors placed certain distance apart along the flow. Traditionally, this was done using a cross-correlation algorithm to estimate the transit time of the coolant, and thus its velocity. This widely used cross-correlation algorithm, however, suffers from the ambiguity in reading of measurements. To alleviate this problem, the transfer function estimation approach was recently proposed which tends to give more accurate results. In this paper, we introduce a new algorithm that can further improve the accuracy in the transit time estimation using an adaptive inverse system model at a higher cost of computation. When real-time computation is a concern, we propose a second algorithm based on an adaptive filtering approach which makes a sound trade-off between accuracy and computation cost. This algorithm incurs less processing time than the first proposed algorithm with higher accuracy than the two aforementioned conventional algorithms.

articleTitle: Anonymous M+1-st price auction using ring signature
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The M+1-st price auction is a style of auction in which the highest M bidders win and pay a uniform price, determined by the M+1-st price. This paper proposes an anonymous M+1-st price auction scheme based on ring signature and homomorphic encryption. It offers the security of bidding price and public verifiability. Meanwhile, both the anonymity of normal bidders and the non-repudiation of malicious bidders are achieved in the scheme.

articleTitle: CNN: Twenty years later
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This speech will present the state-of-the-art of the CNN (Cellular Neural Network) universal chip and its future applications. The speech will last two hours without coffee break. After the speech, a 20 minutes interactive talk among the speaker and audience will be held on the great event: Experiment Verification of Memristor by HP researchers has been done last month. articleTitle: Design and test of a carrier interferometry OFDM system in underwater acoustic channels
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Based on our previous work, a novel design of a carrier interferometry (CI) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system had been tested in a real underwater acoustic channel - the experimental pool in Xiamen University. Since the CI/OFDM system is very sensitive to phase offsets, a simplified 2D estimator is used to reconstruct the channel response at the receiver. The performance of the CI/OFDM and OFDM underwater acoustic communication systems had been compared based on Peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) and BER characteristics. Experiment results showed that the CI/OFDM underwater acoustic communication system could achieve excellent performance.

articleTitle: A reduced-complexity implementation of differential detection for continuous phase modulation in FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: An implement of demodulation for continuous phase modulation is proposed using reduced-complexity method in FPGAs. Viterbi algorithm is implemented to perform sequence correlation and maximum likelihood sequence estimate without reducing states, at the same time a parallel and serial matched filter structure to perform 4096-state correlation. Simulation of the received performance show that the proposed method has reduced complexity without deterioration of the performance.

articleTitle: Performance of fixed channel assignment for uplink transmission and Direct Peer-to-Peer Communications in multihop cellular networks
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we propose a clustered multihop cellular network (cMCN) architecture and study its performance using fixed channel assignment (FCA) scheme for uplink transmission. The proposed cMCN using FCA can be applied with some reuse factors. An analytical model based on Markov chain is developed to analyze its performance and validated through computer simulation. And then, we implement Direct Peer-to-Peer Communication (DC) in cMCN by considering more reasonable conditions in reality. DC means that two calls communicate directly instead of going through base stations. The results show that cMCN with FCA can reduce the call blocking probability significantly as compared with the traditional single-hop cellular networks with FCA and can be further reduced by using DC.

articleTitle: Reducing the complexity of LD-CELP speech coding algorithm using direct vector quantization
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper described the principle of the direct vector quantization (DVQ) algorithm which was applied to simulated decoder module and codebook search module in LD-CELP speech coding algorithm. The synthesis filter in simulated decoder module was replaced by the inverse-perceptual weighting filter, removing the operation of impulse response h(n) in the codebook search module. The result showed that the DVQ algorithm decreased calculation quantity and improved the efficiency of codebook search. The multiplication operation amount of eneragy calculator and time-reversed convolution module could be reduced by 75%, and the addition operation amount could be reduced by 77.78% in an adaptation cycle of four vectors (20 samples), while SNR was equivalent to that of LD-CELP and speech quality had not almost change.

articleTitle: On achievable rates and spectrum allocation in cognitive wireless networks
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper studies the spectrum allocation strategies in cognitive wireless networks. First, spectrum holes with different protection strategies are generalized to the interference temperature strategy and categorized according to their interference constraints. Also, cognitive users are classified according to their ability in obtaining the primary user’s information before actual transmission, which determines their performances in wireless cognitive networks. Then, with the Dirty Paper Coding at the transmitter and the Opportunistic Interference Cancellation at the receiver, the performances of cognitive users in respective spectrum holes are discussed and corresponding capacities of cognitive channels are computed. Following the analysis, several spectrum allocation strategies are proposed. Simulation results show that, one of the proposed strategy dramatically improves the output of the cognitive network without bringing excessive resource consumption load to the system.

articleTitle: A new separation method for Micro-Doppler information of a target with rotating parts
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The classical range-Doppler algorithm canpsilat obtain clear ISAR image of a target with rotating parts. In spectrogram, the micro-Doppler information of the rotor blades is represented as the sinusoidal frequency modulation, whereas the information of main body is depicted as the form of straight lines. So the extraction of micro-Doppler is transformed to the separation of the sinusoids and straight lines. Based on this idea, a simple method of spectrogram cancellation is proposed, which can quickly achieve the purpose of separation and get clear ISAR image of main body. The effectiveness of the algorithm is proved by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Synchronization in time-delayed fractional order chaotic Rossler systems
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we introduced a method to construct controller for the synchronization between two fractional order Rossler systems. The key thought is converting the fractional order system to integer system. The controller uses general linear state error feed backing. Numerical examples are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: General projective synchronization and fractional order chaotic masking scheme
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we introduced a fractional order chaotic masking scheme for secure communication. Based on the General projective synchronization of two coupled fractional chen systems, a popular masking scheme is designed. Numerical example is given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The influence of network traffic correlation on the queueing performance
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, the self-similarity characteristic of network traffic and its influence on the queuing performance are studied. The network simulator OPNET is applied to build a local wired experimental network and a campus wireless network. The queuing performance of these two kinds of network is analyzed based on the M/P/1 queuing model. The simulation results demonstrate the influence of traffic correlation on the queuing performance according to two important parameters, queuing delay and queue length.

articleTitle: A computer-assisted verification of chaos in a Hopfield neural network
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper demonstrates chaos in Hopfield neural networks (HNNS) for certain value assigned to the connection matrix. Based on the topological horseshoe theory and elementary symbolic dynamics, a rigorous computer-assisted verification is offered.

articleTitle: A novel threshold method for 3-band wavelet de-noising
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel threshold method based on the penalized threshold presented by Birge and Massart, the novel threshold is derived in 3-band wavelet domain. Instead of selecting the coefficients which are larger than some threshold, the method merely fixes the number of coefficients we want to keep equal to some value and takes the largest ones. It is effective because the number of wavelet coefficients we kept at each level can be calculated directly and it is adaptive as these values depend on some variables such as α and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, which can be various for particular signal to get the best performance. The experimental results show that in the 3-band wavelet domain, the proposed method represents better characteristics than D.J method in protecting details and improving the signal-to-noise ratio of reconstructed signal. Moreover, the application of the proposed method to simulated ultrasonic signal is demonstrated in the experiment.

articleTitle: A survey of service discovery protocols for mobile ad hoc networks
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: With the enlargement of the network size and application scope of mobile ad hoc networks, the variety and number of service needed by such networks become more and more. Furthermore, in this dynamic environment, different nodes offering different services may enter and leave the network at any time. Efficient and timely service discovery becomes a new task of mobile ad hoc network. Discovery of services is a crucial feature for the usability of mobile ad hoc networks. In this paper, we survey the researches of recent years on service discovery, classify the existing service discovery protocols of mobile ad hoc networks. Moreover, we analyze and compare these protocols. Based on the analysis, further research issues that still need investigation are listed.

articleTitle: An estimation scheme for integer frequency offsets based on pilot channel estimation in wireless OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel frequency synchronizator for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems over multipath fading channels. With the help of pilot chips and channel estimates in frequency domain, we can analyze the delay power spectrum (DPS) of multipath channels and estimate the integer carrier frequency offset (CFO). Furthermore, the pseudo noise (PN) pilot chips are proposed to extend the estimation range. We verify our algorithm by Monte Carlo simulation, and the results show high accuracy and robustness in a wide range of velocities and signal to noise ratios (SNRs).

articleTitle: Sensor networks: Motivations, implementations and applications
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Due to advances in micro-sensors, wireless networking, and embedded processing, ad-hoc networks of sensors (popularly known as sensor networks) are becoming increasingly available for commercial, industrial, and military applications such as health and environmental monitoring (e.g., patient care, traffic, habitat, pollutant), industrial sensing and diagnostics (e.g., factory automation, appliances), infrastructures (e.g., power grids, water distribution, waste disposal, security), and battlefield awareness (e.g., detection, localization, multi-target tracking). In this presentation, we will first provide a brief history and motivations on sensor network. Then we will discuss various technical aspects covering theory, implementation, system, and applications. Topics in networking and protocols, embedded systems, distributed processing, and signal/array processing will be considered. We will consider the challenges and potentials of sensor networks both at the technological and application points of view.

articleTitle: Passivity analysis of T-S Fuzzy-model-based uncertain switched systems with delays
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the passivity problem of T-S fuzzy-model-based switched systems with time-varying delay and uncertainties. By using the Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional method, together with linear matrix inequality approach, the authors first establish the passivity conditions for such class of switched nonlinear systems. These results are easy to be verified and are applicable to any smooth continuous-time switched nonlinear systems.

articleTitle: DSO-based signal reconstruction of time-interleaved
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Time-interleaved ADC system is an effective way to implement a high-sampling-rate ADC with relatively slow circuits in DSO(Digital Storage Oscilloscopes). However, the mismatch such as offset, gain and time mismatches among channel ADCs, cause distortion in sampling signal. In this paper, we present a method for estimation and compensation of offset and gain errors, and use a formula to reconstruct the sampling signal. Numerical simulations are used to validate the proposed compensation and reconstruction algorithm. The major advantage of this technique is that all the calibration and reconstruction processes are carried out in a simple way which will not cost too much time to remove the errors, and it can greatly improve the SFDR and SNR of ADCs.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of Reconfigurable Stream Processor in multimedia applications
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper proposed a Reconfigurable Stream Processor applied in multimedia applications. Based on the unique parallel stream processing framework and optimized algorithm mapping method, the reconfigurable processor exploits the parallelism of complex algorithms and provides a high flexibility during run-time to adapt to various applications. The architecture of processor is implemented and verified on the development board of ARM926EJS plus Xilinx Virtex-4XC4VLX80. A H.264 video codec is implemented to verify the reconfigurable architecture, achieving 58%~130% speed boost compared with traditional reconfigurable architectures such as MorphoSys and PACT.

articleTitle: Spatially selective STBC-VBLAST in MIMO communication system
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a new algorithm of MIMO system has been proposed by applying antenna selection into hybrid STBC-VBLAST architecture. It has been confirmed that there is an outstanding performance improvement even for simple receiver with ZF and MMSE decoder. Furthermore, in order to decrease the complexity in MIMO-OFDM systems configured with hybrid STBC-VBLAST, a simplified version of the aforementioned algorithm is proposed, which can be proved to realize antenna selection without significant performance deterioration.

articleTitle: Configuration of floorplan and placement algorithm using horizontal and vertical contour based on single sequence
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The single-sequence (simply SS) is an effective and efficient representation of non-slicing floorplan, which utilizes permutation of integers 1, 2, 3<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">hellip</sub>, n to represent sets of ABLR-relations (above, below, left-of, right-of) that hold among n objects on the plane without overlapping. For fast decoding SS code, horizontal and vertical contours (HVC) are introduced. From geometrical information kept in HVC, not only corresponding configuration of floorplan but also placement can be realized simultaneously in linear time. Example of configuration of floorplan and experimental results on MCNC benchmarks showed the promising results of our proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Frequency offset and phase noise influence and its compensation in the DFT-spread OFDM system
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, frequency offset and phase noise influence and its compensation technique are discussed in the DFT-spread OFDM system. Simulation results show that DFT-spread OFDM introduces more interference than OFDM because of DFT spreading phase offset mismatch caused by frequency offset and random phase noise. Data conjugate ICI self-cancellation method is suggested to improve system performance.

articleTitle: A projected WRLA super-resolution algorithm for PMMW imaging
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Images acquired from Passive Millimeter-Wave (PMMW) radiometer have poor resolution due to limited aperture dimension. Therefore, Super-Resolution Algorithm (SRA) is a key component for PMMW imager. SRA realizes spectrum extrapolation, however, spectrum in-band is deteriorated too. Wiener-Richardson-Lucy Algorithm (WRLA) recovers spectrum in-band by Wiener filter, and extrapolates spectrum out-of-band by Richardson-Lucy Algorithm (RLA). WRLA can avoid spectrum deterioration in passband, but its ability for spectrum extrapolation is limited also. We propose an improved algorithm to solve this problem. This algorithm, which has built constraints according to characteristics of PMMW imaging, uses Projection-Onto-Convex-Sets (POCS) technique to enhance the WRLA’s performance, so it is termed as POCS-WRLA.

articleTitle: Research in global motion estimation for target segmention
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Global Motion Estimation is still dilemma for researchers hard to determine a tradeoff between accuracy and computer complexity. This paper presents a three steps algorithm to get this tradeoff. First it uses the law of inertia for camera to quicken the Black Matching Algorithm. The last two steps are using recursive statistic error to get better affine model parameter. The simulation results that this algorithm can deal with the camera shift, rotation and scaling, as well as taking less time.

articleTitle: Adaptive Load-balancing in WDM mesh networks with partial traffic information
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Valiant load-balancing [1] (VLB) has attracted considerable research interest in recent years, as it guarantees 100% throughput for any traffic matrix satisfying hose model[2] constraints without obtaining precise traffic matrix. However, when the traffic variation tends to be gentle, the measurement of traffic demands between certain node pairs becomes feasible. Then it is likely to adjust the VLB scheme to access significant reduction in propagation delay. This paper studies adaptive load-balancing (ALB) in WDM networks provided that the traffic matrix is partially known during the operation time, which can be solved in two steps: 1) construct VLB architecture for a given WDM network; 2) route all the traffic demands in the architecture with a partially known traffic matrix. We first propose a novel heuristic termed MNC (Maximizing Network Capability) to structure a VLB WDM network. Then a heuristic ADT (Adding Direct Traffic) is proposed to minimize average propagation delay with traffic grooming [3][4][5]. Simulation results show that MNC costs less than the previous heuristics and ADT reaches notable improvement in propagation delay.

Index Terms: Pairs Of Nodes In The Network

articleTitle: Image simulation of PMMW based on multibeam reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a new approach is described to generate passive millimeter-wave (PMMW) simulation image for multibeam reflector antenna (MBA). This approach includes material radiation parameter database building, multibeam antenna pattern computing and system scanning method design. As an efficient way to predict the performance of a PMMW imager, PMMW imaging simulation is a key component for system design.

articleTitle: Amplitude statistical analysis of Ku-Band SAR ground clutter data
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The objective of this paper is to provide an analysis of the amplitude statistics of Ku-Band SAR ground clutter data using Weibull, Gamma, K and lognormal distribution. Their goodness-of-fit have been carried out by Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) test after the estimation of the distribution parameters. The results show that Gamma distribution approximates much better the value of the empirical probability density function(PDF) for the agricultural terrain;K distribution approximates much better the value of the empirical PDF for the grass terrains; Lognormal distribution approximates much better the value of the empirical PDF for the building and hurst blocks.

articleTitle: ZP-OFDM broadcasting systems with insufficient Guard Interval
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The conventional over-lapping-add equalizer for ZP-OFDM based broadcasting systems fails to eliminate the ISI and ICI introduced by multipath propagation when the channel impulse response (CIR) length exceeds the duration of guard interval (GI). We propose, in this paper, a new equalization scheme for the suppression of insufficient GI generated interference using inherent diversity property of ZP-OFDM signal. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can effectively recovers the contaminated ZP-OFDM signal.

articleTitle: Detection performance of PMMW image
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: We study the effect of PMMW(passive millimeter wave) radiometer parameters and targetpsilas characteristics on detection distance based on analyzing the rang equation of PMMW radiometer and raise the enhancing method of MMW passive detection function and the direction of PMMW radiometric characteristics control from PMMW image with using the statistical method.

articleTitle: Implementation and optimization of I-frame in AVS1-P2 decoder based on DSP
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: AVS1-P2 is Chinese next-generation video coding standard and becomes one of the international IPTV standards in 2007. In this paper we present various techniques used to implement AVS video decoder on Texas Instruments’ DM642 DSP. And propose optimization methods for AVS1-P2 I-frame decoding. The experimental result shows that our design improves the performance a lot without any loss in video quality. It demonstrates the success of our techniques. The optimization techniques used for I-frame decoding are also suitable for P-frame and B-frame decoding in AVS1-P2 decoder.

articleTitle: A 13-bit CMOS pipeline analog-to-digital converter with improved sampling circuits
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A 13-bit CMOS pipeline analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with improved sampling circuits is proposed. In the first pipeline stage, the high frequency performance of the sampling circuit is improved by reducing the on-resistances of the switches and the time skew between the sampling capacitors and the comparators. In the subsequent stages, the conventional sampling circuit is modified for low power design by reducing the loading of the residue amplifier. The prototype ADC has been fabricated in a 0.18-μm CMOS process. With a 2.4-MHz input and 2.5-MHz sampling rate, the measured peak SNDR and SFDR are 75.26 dB and 90.46 dBc respectively. And when the input frequency increases to 15.4 MHz, this converter still achieves a 70.36 dB SNDR and a 93.9 dBc SFDR. Furthermore, it is verified by code density test that the first stage with the improved sampling circuit still functions correctly with the input frequency up to 282 MHz. The power consumption including output pad drivers is 21 mW at 2.7-V power supply.

articleTitle: The chaotic disturbance of UAV system’s communication and coping strategy
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The chaotic disturbance phenomenon will occur in peculiar circumstances to the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) system. In this paper, the authors have discussed the condition of this phenomenon, analyzed its causes through the entire environment simulation and the concrete flight practice, and applied the on-line strategy to establish a mathematical model according to the system disturbance factor. A mathematical relation among the chaotic factors of this peculiar phenomenon has been given with regard to the experiments, and finally a solution is proposed in view of the disturbance factorpsilas characteristics, moreover, the validity of this plan is further confirmed through the simulation and the flight practice.

articleTitle: Two novel algorithms for blind equalization of cross-QAM signals
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents two novel blind equalization algorithms suitable for cross-QAM signals. Based on the framework of the constant cross algorithm (CXA), the improved constant cross algorithm (ICXA) is obtained by introducing multiple contours and adding a control function in the weight update. Furthermore, in order to get better performance, Modified ICXA is obtained by adding a constellation-matched error (CME) term in the cost function of the ICXA. In the MICXA, the ICXA term provides global convergence and the CME term helps to decrease the residual error and accelerate convergence. The equalization performance of the proposed algorithms demonstrated by the simulation result for 32-QAM signal constellation proves that the efficacy of the novel algorithms is better than the existing CXA.

articleTitle: EBETX: An energy-balanced reliable routing metric method for wireless sensor network
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: An energy-balanced reliable routing metric method based on ETX was proposed, which aimed at the limited energy and the special requirement of transmission reliability for wireless sensor network. This method improves the ETX routing metric method. It avoids the data packets transmit along the lower energy path, and selects the path which has more surplus energy. Thus, it makes the energy of the nodes in the network keep balance. Simulation results show that this method can prolong the lifetime of the network and implement the effective balance of transmission reliability and energy balance.

articleTitle: Automatic pair-matching method for estimating 2-D angle of arrival
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we propose an automatic pair-matching method for two-dimensional (2-D) angle estimation. Unlike some classical pair-matching methods requiring a complex process, this method utilizes the corresponding combinations of the elevation and azimuth angles emerging in the cross-correlation matrix of two uniform linear arrays (ULAs) to achieve automatic pairing. Computer simulations are used to show the performance of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: An improved NSSK protocol and its security analysis based on logic approach
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Authentication protocol is a very important kind of protocol in network environment, and formal analysis is the key method to guarantee its security properties. Needham-Schroeder Shared-Key (NSSK) protocol is considered as one of the earliest and very important authentication protocol. The paper proposed a new improved version of NSSK protocol by modifying message format and decreasing message flows, and it also analysed the security of the proposed protocol by utilizing the formal approach based on logic. The analysis results reveal that the proposed protocol achieves the expectative authentication goals.

articleTitle: A survivability over security (SOS) model for computer network inspired by biological immunology and gene mutation
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Computer virus severely threats network security and new virus emerges while the old one is still spreading. In this paper, inspired by natural immune system and biological evolution theory, we propose a novel architecture for the computer network to improve its security and survivability. Borrowing methods from the complex network theory and epidemiology, some factors involved in the network survivability are analyzed, including network topology, distribution of immune node, the life-span of antigen and antibody and gene service mutation etc. A scale-free network model, characterized by Internet etc., is also proposed to study the sensitivity of those factors.

articleTitle: Performance of peak cancellation for PAPR reduction in OFDM system
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: High peak to average power ratio (PAPR) is one of the main disadvantages of OFDM. Clipping can reduce the PAPR but suffers from high out-of-band distortion. Recently, peak cancellation is introduced to reduce the out-of-band radiation with a band-limited cancellation function. In this paper, a set of windowing function is applied as the cancellation function. Furthermore, the cancellation function is windowed into limited number of samples, and the performance of sinc function with different number of limited samples is investigated. Simulation results show that peak cancellation with a limited-sample sinc function can achieve better PAPR reduction performance with lower complexity.

articleTitle: A distributed remote monitoring system based on ARM for production lines
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: A distributed remote monitoring system is developed for production lines in this paper. The system architecture and the design of system hardware and software are also presented. This monitoring system is composed of field control units, central monitor and remote monitoring computer. The central monitor which adopts Samsungpsilas S3C44B0X chip based on ARM7TDMI kernel as controller is the core of the whole system. In the central monitor, uClinux operating system and JFFS2 file system are transplanted to receive and store the real-time data of production lines collected by field control units. Furthermore, the real time monitoring of production lines through Internet could be successfully realized by transplanting embedded web server onto the central monitor.

articleTitle: Improved digital average current control of buck converter with dual-edge modulation
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper explores digital average current (DAC) control buck converter with dual-edge modulation (trailing-triangle modulation and leading-triangle modulation). It is found that DAC control with dual-edge modulation doesn’t have sub-oscillation problems. As the same as conventional digital control of switching dc-dc converter, there is also one switching cycle time delay between sampling and corresponding duty ratio updating in DAC control algorithm. To overcome this time delay of DAC control, an improved digital average current (IDAC) control is then proposed and studied. The control laws of the proposed digital algorithms are discussed and compared. Simulation results are given to further verify the analysis results.

articleTitle: Fabrication of micro/nano optical wires with modified fiber-drawing process
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Silica micro/nano optical wires (MNOWs) with diameter down to several hundred nanometers were obtained by employing a modified fiber drawing process, which exhibited an average optical propagation loss of less than 1.0dB/mm.

articleTitle: 0.13μm 1.0V–1.5V supply digital blocks for 40-Gb/s optical communication systems
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Low supply digital blocks for OC-768/STM-256 optical communication systems such as 1:2 demultiplexer (DEMUX), 2:1 multiplexer (MUX), 2:1 frequency divider and data decision circuit in 0.13 mum CMOS are presented. All proposed blocks are based on fully differential MOS current-mode logic (CML). Multi-stage output buffers are used to drive the external 50 Omega loads. On-chip shunt peaking (SP) inductors and split resistor (SR) loads are used to boost the bandwidth. High output resistance current sources are employed to achieve flat current source characteristic and allow the designed ICs to operate stably with wide process, voltage and temperature (PVT) variations. The main contribution of this work is that four proposed circuits can work at 40-Gb/s and beyond under a 1 V supply and consume low currents.

articleTitle: Experimental investigations and behavior modeling for monolithic quasi-class E SiGe PA linearization
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: We have developed a modified bias-dependent Cann’s model and performed IC design and hardware experiments to study the linearization of a highly-efficient monolithic quasi-class E SiGe power amplifier (PA) IC using both Envelope-Tracking (ET) and Envelope-Elimination-and-Restoration (EER) techniques. Our simple PA behavior model fits the measured SiGe PA IC data very well across a wide range of bias and supply voltages. Both measurement and simulations show that the ET-linearized PA system is significantly less sensitive to the timing misalignment between the amplitude and the RF signal path than the EER-linearized PA system. Our experimental results also show that ET successfully linearized the SiGe PA to pass the stringent EDGE transmit mask at 900MHz, while EER could not. Simulations also predict that the optimal timing alignment for ET linearization can be achieved at PA base bias voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bb</inf>=0.55–0.6V, which is consistent with our measurement results as well.

articleTitle: An MLD scheme for interference suppression based on noise subspace projection for MIMO-OSTBCs system
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents an interference suppression reception scheme for the multiple input multiple output (MIMO) communication systems using orthogonal space-time block codes (OSTBCs) in strong interference scenario. Based on the noise subspace projection, the maximum likelihood decoding (MLD) for OSTBCs can be achieved by simple linear processing in this scheme. Moreover, the approach to obtain the efficient channel state information (CSI) in strong interference scenario is also included in this proposed scheme. The simulation results are given to verify the interference suppression ability of the proposed scheme. Compared with other suppression scheme, the proposed scheme has better SER performance and is more flexible in practical applications.

articleTitle: The bidirectional-based SRMC for hierarchical B frame in scalable video coding
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: From System-on-chip (SOC) perspective, memory bandwidth plays an important role in system performance for video coding applications. Owing to the locality of video data, the data reuse scheme is widely applied to reduce the memory bandwidth requirement. For further improvement of performance, frame-based data reuse scheme, single reference frame and multiple current macroblocks (SRMC), can provide more efficient solution; however, the coding efficiency could be sacrificed. For scalable video coding (SVC), the coding efficiency is more precious than it of single layer coding scheme. For this reason, the bidirectional-based SRMC is proposed for hierarchical B frame in SVC. The proposed method efficiently stores temporary backward or forward prediction information for final mode decision. Based on our method, the saved ratio of memory bandwidth is as high as 34% to 65% under various display specifications.

articleTitle: Simulation research on P-Aloha protocol in underwater acoustic network based on OPNET
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The paper mainly research on the performance of the application of P-Aloha in underwater acoustic network. The OPNET-based modeling of the underwater acoustic channel of the underwater acoustic network is first presented in the paper, and the P-Aloha protocol is also modeled. The different performance of the protocol in underwater and atmospheric wireless environment is compared in the simulation results. The performance of protocol in underwater acoustic network is improved by setting the optimal propagation delay parameter.

articleTitle: Secure and robust audio watermarking scheme based on discrete fractional transform
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The traditional transform domain watermarking schemes are insecure for publicity characteristic of transform itself. Aimming at this, a secret discrete fractional Sine transform (DFRST) domain audio watermarking scheme is proposed in this paper. The undeterminate angle of DFRST is utilized and the security of the proposed scheme is enhanced using chaotic sequences. Experimental results show the proposed secure scheme is imperceptible and robust against various signal processing attacks.

articleTitle: An effective AS-FIFO design for Multiple Asynchronous Clock data transmission
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper presents an effective design of a asynchronous FIFO circuit for multiple asynchronous clocks data transmission. The dual synchronization and gray code are proposed. According to experiments, the probability of metastability is reduced effectively. In the simulation the proposed circuits can operate at a clock rate of 256 MHz while in writing and 329 MHz in reading and is implemented in ALTERA Cyclone device. The simulation indicates that this design will have a wide application for multiple asynchronous clocks data transmission in SoPC or ASIC design.

articleTitle: Analysis of opportunistic access in the spectrum sharing system with heterogeneous secondary users
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: For the purpose of increasing the utilization efficiency of spectrum, secondary usage method of the licensed spectrum has been explored. In this paper, based on the concept of spectrum pooling, we propose a spectrum sharing system with opportunistic accesses. In order to satisfy with the realistic applications, we define heterogeneous secondary users (non-real-time and real-time services) with different quality-of-service (QoS) requirements in our system model. Since each primary userpsilas requiring channel may be occupied by different types of secondary user, the primary user uses different schemes to solve the collision. Numerical results show that our model can obtain a better tradeoff between increasing the spectrum utilization and guaranteeing the primary userpsilas access priority.

articleTitle: Impulsive control of a class of uncertain systems with small time delay
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper studies impulsive control of a class of uncertain systems with small time delay. Some robust stability criteria for impulsive delay differential system are presented, based on which the impulsive control law can be easily designed. Our technique depends on Lyapunov’s direct method and comparison principle. Finally, we present the estimate of the upper bound of the uncertain constant time delay and impulse interval for robust asymptotically stable impulsive control.

articleTitle: On decoding of quadratic residue codes with irreducible generator polynomials
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, a simple decoding scheme for the quadratic residue codes that utilize extended Euclid’s algorithm is proposed. This decoding method is based on the property of the syndrome polynomial to obtain the error-locator polynomial. Moreover, the simulation results for comparing the new decoding method with a proposed method are given.

articleTitle: The radiation characteristics of Partial SOI VDMOS
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The partial SOI structure of VDMOS is proposed in paper. The transient radiation and single-event-effect characteristics of the device are discussed. The results are shown that the transient radiation toleration of the partial SOI VDMOS is twice times than that of the conventional VDMOS with the same excellent power characteristics, single-event-effect toleration of the partial SOI VDMOS is more than that of the conventional VDMOS, and the critical LET of the partial SOI VDMOS is two times than the conventional VDMOS.

articleTitle: Using data fusion for awareness of intrusion in large-scale network
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Network security situation awareness is a hot research realm in the area of network security, which helps security analysts to solve the challenges they encounter. This paper presents the network characteristic attributes to describe the state of large-scale network; Then the fusion algorithm deal with statistical info, the experimental result has shown the algorithm can meet the large-scale network information processing need. An anomaly detection model based on the multi-feature similarity in large-scale network is proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Necessary and sufficient conditions for bounded control of positive systems
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the bounded control of positive systems, both continuous- and discrete-time ones. The control is under boundedness constraint, which means that both the input and the states of the closed-loop system are bounded and positive (the original systems are not necessarily positive). The main contribution lies in two aspects. First, a necessary and sufficient condition is provided for the bounded control of continuous-time systems. Second, a similar condition is also established for the discrete-time systems. All the controllers are explicitly constructed if existent and all the results are formulated as linear programming problems, hence easy to be verified.

articleTitle: Image registration based on feature extraction and voting strategy
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In this paper, we develop a coarse-to-fine method for the registration of the reference and target images, involving the 2D rigid transformation. The proposed method consists of four steps: utilizing Harris corner detector to extract the feature points in the reference and target images; corresponding these points by a novel feature points match algorithm based on voting strategy, which efficiently eliminates the false and unstable matches; estimating the transformation parameters with the corresponded feature points; refining the transformation parameters with the window-based method. Experimental results have demonstrated that the proposed method is able to achieve high accuracy and robustness with low computational burden.

articleTitle: Adaptive GOP structure determination in hierarchical B picture coding for the extension of H.264/AVC
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: The hierarchical B-picture coding is introduced into the extension of H.264/AVC in order to improve coding performance and provide strong temporal scalability as well. In general, coding performance is affected by the content variation in GOP. Therefore, the ways to determine the size of GOP (group of picture) is a critical problem for video coding. In this paper, the adaptive GOP structure determination scheme is proposed to select the appropriate GOP size with content complexity consideration. Experimental results show that the proposed method can provide better PSNR performance compared to the highest GOP setting in the existing hierarchical B-picture coding of H.264/AVC.

articleTitle: An improved FSM-based method for BGP protocol conformance testing
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: In protocol engineering area, conformance testing is a very important step. The purpose of conformance testing is to determine to what extent a single implementation of a particular standard conforms to the individual requirements of that standard. The Finite State Machine (FSM) model is usually used in protocol conformance testing. In this paper, an improved FSM-based method is introduced to generate the conformance test sequences of BGP protocol. This FSM-based method is a mixture version of Unique Input Output (UIO) method and T method. The UIO method has better capability than T method, but the length of conformance test sequences of that is much longer. The simulation results have shown that the improved method has better fault coverage than UIO method, while the length of the test sequences is close to T method.

articleTitle: Implement of channel estimation for OFDM communicaton system under UWA channel
publicationTitle: 2008 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems
abstract: Underwater acoustic (UWA) channel is a time-space-frequency varying channel. Coherent detection requires channel estimation in Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) system. In this paper, the channel estimation methods based on pilot for OFDM UWA system are investigated.
